summary: Hydrate scalar item IDs before upsert so `sync` actually stores HN stories/updates instead of dropping every row.
reason: The HN Firebase list endpoints wired into sync (/jobstories.json, /updates.json) return bare scalar item IDs, not objects. The generic sync pipeline extracts a primary key from object fields, so every scalar item was dropped (sync_anomaly all_items_failed_id_extraction, stored=0) — the symptom reported in printing-press-library#1348. Added an itemHydration map plus hydrateScalarItems/scalarItemID helpers in internal/cli/sync.go that fetch each ID's full object from /item/<id>.json before upsert; failed hydrations are folded into the existing extract-failure accounting. The deeper fix belongs upstream in CLI Printing Press: the profiler should recognize fetch-IDs-then-hydrate APIs and emit a hydration pattern (e.g. via an x-hydrate / x-resource-id annotation) rather than wiring scalar-ID list endpoints into the object-shaped sync path.
validated_outcome: go build ./..., go vet ./internal/cli/, and gofmt are clean. Unit tests in internal/cli/sync_hydration_test.go pass and cover scalar-ID detection, ID->object hydration, unfetchable-ID failure counting, and object/unknown-resource pass-through. End-to-end `hackernews-pp-cli sync --resources stories --max-pages 1` against the live public Firebase API now reports {"event":"sync_summary","total_records":31,...} with zero sync_anomaly events (previously 0 stored), and `search local` returns the hydrated rows — confirming the #1348 symptom is resolved. Note: internal/store TestMigrate_ConcurrentFreshDB is pre-existing flaky (SQLITE_BUSY on concurrent Open) and unrelated to this change.
